Expurgate

/EKS-per-gayt/ - the stress falls on EKS · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Expurgate means to remove the offensive or objectionable parts of a text.

The anthology's editors expurgated the sailors' shanties, so the printed verses end two lines before the sailors did.

Worked Example

Before the school broadcast, the drama teacher expurgated the radio play, cutting the duel and the tavern brawl but keeping every turn of the plot intact.

Expurgate is narrower than edit or shorten because it targets only what might offend — the duel and the brawl went, not because the play was too long, but to make a clean version for young ears.

How Expurgate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

censor

censor: suppress content by authority — a state or platform forbidding it

bowdlerize

bowdlerize: expurgate prudishly — named for Thomas Bowdler's scrubbed Shakespeare

Antonyms

restore

restore: put the removed passages back in place

retain

retain: keep the disputed passages where they stand

How Strong Is It? — soften → cut → expurgate

soften vs. expurgate

soften vs. expurgate: Soften is the lightest touch — the rough joke stays in, just gentler by a word or two.

cut vs. expurgate

cut vs. expurgate: Cut is stronger than soften but narrower than expurgate: you cut one scene, while expurgating means combing the whole work and stripping every part that could offend.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of expurgate.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ex-

Prefix — ex-: out

Root — purg

Root — purg: to cleanse (Latin purgare)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: verb ending: to make or do

Put it together

Put it together: Ex- (out) + purg (to cleanse, from Latin purgare) + -ate (verb ending) = to cleanse out — to wash the objectionable matter out of a text. The same root gives purge, which you will meet in this unit's reference list, and purgatory, the place where souls were said to be scrubbed clean. An expurgated edition has been through the wash.

Use the root in a new word: purgatory

Use the root in a new word: purgatory: Medieval paintings show purgatory as a mountain the soul climbs while its faults burn away.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / editorial

Expurgate is an editor's word, and a precise one: the cuts aim at offense, not length. Truncate, taught in this unit, shortens by lopping off an end; expunge, also in this unit, annihilates an entry from a record. Censor is the heavier cousin — an authority forbidding content — where expurgating produces a cleaned edition that still gets published.
